finds.title: FIESTAWARE VINTAGE TEAPOT
finds.note: text-triage L1: Fiesta medium teapot, footed, vintage shape. Ask: base photo (vintage ink "fiesta HLC USA" lowercase vs Post-86 in-mold FIESTA (R)), daylight photo beside a white plate, close-up of spout chip. Buy at $30 only if medium green and vintage mark.

finds.title: old comic book collection (16)
finds.note: text-triage L3: 16 silver-age comics for $25: Batman 80-Page Giants #185 (G-27, Nov 1966), #187 (G-30, Jan 1967, "Best of Batman"), #193 (G-37, Aug 1967); Detective Comics #367 (Sept 1967 jigsaw cover) and the "Batman's Last Hour" Detective (~#366); 2 Adventure Comics Superboy & Legion (~#340s); Gold Key Tarzan x2, Top Cat, Ruff & Reddy, Archie, Betty & Me, Devil Kids, New Terrytoons, Classics Illustrated Jungle Book. Low-end resale ~$150 for the lot (no comp; giants ~$20-40 each raw VG). Ask: confirm all 16 are pictured, no cut coupons/missing pages, cover/spine condition close-ups (back covers). tp_query: "Batman 80 page giant 185", "Batman 187 giant", "Detective Comics 367", "Adventure Comics Legion 1966 lot".

finds.title: VINTAGE FABERGE ENAMEL EGG PENDANT
finds.note: text-triage L1: Red/green enamel egg pendant on wire collar sold as "Faberge"; looks like a Faberge-style souvenir (no hallmark visible). Real Faberge/Victor Mayer egg pendants carry FABERGE + VM + 18K/925 marks on the cap/bail. Ask: macro of the cap/bail and egg back for marks; if none, kill.

finds.title: *Antique fiddle bow*
finds.note: text-triage F3: 29.5" violin bow, round pernambuco-colored stick, ebony frog with nickel mounts and pearl eye, silver-wire wrap, 48.8 g (light); seller says "possibly Mirecourt c.1920s". 12 photos show no brand stamp. Ask for a sharp photo of the stick just above the frog on both sides for a fire-brand (e.g. "Bazin", "Ouchard", "Mirecourt", vs "Germany"/"Nürnberger"/blank) and whether the mounts are nickel or silver. Unstamped German trade bow ~$80–120 does not clear; a stamped Mirecourt workshop bow does. violin-bows comp is ebay-active ($265 asking), no sold comp

finds.title: 1917 Elgin pocket watch
finds.note: text-triage F4: 1917 Elgin small-size HUNTER case watch, engraved scroll lid, inner lid engraved presentation "...from Father & Mother...", seller says it runs. Value hinges on the case: ask for a clear photo of the stamps inside the back lid - solid "14K" (+ U.S. Assay/eagle or maker Dueber/Wadsworth/Keystone) vs "Guaranteed 20/25 years" gold-filled - plus movement grade/jewels and the case weight. Entry: any solid 10K/14K case bought <= $200 is a strong buy; GF = $80-150 -> pass.

finds.title: Vintage Schramberg German Vase
finds.note: text-triage L1: SMF Schramberg (Schramberger Majolikafabrik) hand-painted Art Deco pitcher (seller calls it a vase), 6", shield mark "Handpainted SMF Germany" (1920s-30s). Value hinges on whether the decor is an Eva Zeisel-era (1928-30) design. Ask: photo of base for a painted 4-digit decor/pattern number and form number; confirm no chips/crazing; offer ~$20. No comp: low $60 if generic SMF deco -> fails; Zeisel-attributed decor could be $150+.

finds.title: Vintage Christmas Brooch Pins Lots
finds.note: text-triage F2: Christmas pin lots priced per sub-lot; the "Christmas Tree lot" ($25) has 5 enamel/rhinestone trees + Danforth pewter scatter pin on card. Ask for photos of the BACK of each tree pin: looking for Eisenberg (Eisenberg Ice script), Hollycraft (dated), Weiss, Original by Robert, ART, Mylu. Unsigned = kill. If 1-2 signed est $70-90 for the tree lot.

finds.title: vintage microsecope

finds.title: Antique Leitz Brass Compound Monocular Microscope 11inches high

finds.title: Real civil war belt buckle
finds.note: eye-first: US oval belt plate (waist-belt size), stamped brass face, lead-filled back with two brass arrowhead hooks and one tongue/bar hook, which is the correct 1860s Model 1839/1863 construction. Reproductions copy this exactly, and the bright crystalline 'spangled' lead in photos 2-3 is a common tell of a modern recast; originals usually show dull, smooth grey oxidized lead and wear at the hooks. Ask: exact size (3.5 x 2.2 in large vs 2.75 in small), any maker stamp on the hooks or lead (e.g., 'BOYD', 'J.H. SMITH'), and the source/provenance (dug or family). Buy only if the lead is dull an

finds.note: eye-first: Working wood decoy, 12 in, glass eyes, screwed-on keel weight strip, original worn and crazed paint, separate dowelled head. A coastal scoter brings more than the $80 unmarked-decoy median. finds.note: eye-first: Pair of hollow?/solid wood working bluebill (scaup) drake decoys from Fruitland MD (Lower Eastern Shore -- Crisfield/Ward Bros country). Ward & Bro.', owner brands, keel/lead weight), the neck joint (dowelled head, replaced?), eyes (glass vs tack vs painted), and whether paint is original. Buy only if a named Lower Shore carver mark appears.

Photos show: The Arabian Prince 'It Ain't Tough' (Rapsur RP 10005; Arabian Prince was a founding NWA member), Fila Fresh Crew 'Fear Of The Rap' (Get Live MRC-1089; Dr. Dre/D.O.C.-related Dallas crew), The Triple Threat Three 'M.P.G. Rap' (Sound of Sacramento SAT-2010, with a Dr. Dre credit), Unknown DJ 'Break-Down' (Techno Hop), The Future M.C.'s 'We Are The Future' (Flash 001) and 'Erotic' (Hitt's RAPP-001), Future Flash/King M.C. 'State of Shock', The Mistress & DJ Madame E 'I

finds.title: Captain Beefheart Magic Band Trout Mask Replica vinyl record album
finds.note: eye-first: Captain Beefheart Trout Mask Replica 2LP, pink Straight label 2 STS 1053 (1969 US original, not the Reprise reissue). At $100 needs ~$250 resale; no comp. Ask: gatefold cover condition, vinyl grade, inner sleeves; offer $60. Est low end, no comp.

finds.title: Vintage Scholastic 65 Graduation pendant / charm
finds.note: eye-first: 1965 class-year scroll charm ('65' plaque with scroll ends, coiled bail; 'Scholastic' style), seller calls it gold-tone but back/bail shows no visible mark at photo resolution. Class charms of this form were commonly made in 10K. Ask: close-up of back, bail and jump ring for '10K'/'1/20 10K GF'/maker mark (Balfour, Jostens, Herff Jones) and weight in grams. If 10K and ~2g, melt ~$80-100 (no comp); if GF, ~$5.

finds.title: Champagne capsules
finds.note: eye-first: About 180 champagne capsules (plaques de muselet), collected in the early-1980s LA sommelier trade, about 90% different; visible Moet, Mumm and coloured/portrait caps; the seller mentions 'rare ones from the Taittinger collection'. Light to ship. Ask: (1) is $5 the price for the whole lot or per capsule; (2) a count; (3) close-ups of the Taittinger and any portrait/numbered or pre-1980 caps (Krug, Salon, Dom Perignon, Cristal and old non-French caps are the ones capsule collectors pay for). At $5 for the lot, about $80 resale passes. No comp, so the estimate is low-end.

finds.title: Vintage Old Man Portrait Mina Moiseyev 1882 Print
finds.note: golden-egg review: Hand-painted oil on hardboard (~12x9) copy of Ivan Kramskoi's 'Mina Moiseyev' (1882, State Russian Museum), signed 'N. Ivanov' upper left; listing wrongly calls it a print — Mislisted as 'Licensed Reprint' so few bidders; small/light, cheap to ship. Profit only if resold as hand-painted oil copy; not an egg.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Disney Sleeping Beauty (1959) production cel of Flora, Fauna and Merryweather, Art Corner-style mat — Turn over: look for gold Disneyland Art Corner sticker on back of mat; confirm hand-painted cel (raised paint, layered acetate) vs. sericel/print; check paint lifting. Buy if under ~$500.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Bubble Up 'kiss of lemon, kiss of lime' lighted bubble-glass advertising wall clock (Pam-style, c.1950s-60s) — Check back for Pam Clock Co. (New Rochelle NY) label, that it lights and runs, glass uncracked, no rust on can. Worth it under ~$150.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Disneyland Art Corner production cel, Sleeping Beauty (1959): Briar Rose/Aurora seated with rabbit and two squirrels, matted. — Company lists the Sleeping Beauty cels in the description (Aurora, woodland creatures, fairies, Prince Phillip), so they know it; only worth the trip if tagged under ~$1,000. Check the back for the gold Art Corner sticker/certificate, paint lifting, and that the cel is hand-inked (not a sericel/litho). Go Wed opening 9am.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Watercolor signed "A J Merrill" lower left, Native woman/pueblo scene with adobe and tree; likely Arthur J. Merrill (1885-1973), Taos/Southwest watercolorist with a work in the Harwood Museum. — Marginal: buy only if tagged under ~$100. Confirm it is a hand-painted watercolor (not print), look for a date next to the signature (1930s-40s best) and any Taos/New Mexico label on the back. Sale description does not mention art, so likely priced as decor.

estate-sale golden-egg review: R.C. Gorman hand-pulled lithograph of a seated shawled woman with fringe, pencil-signed "R.C. Gorman" and dated (looks like 1977) lower left, pencil edition number lower right (looks like x/75), deckle edges, framed. — Buy under ~$150. Confirm pencil (not plate-printed) signature and edition number, deckle-edge lithograph paper (not offset poster - look for halftone dots with a loupe), and note title/printer chop (Tamarind/Western Graphics) on back. Frame ~30x38 in, fits passenger seat/back seat. Company field is blank: check the sale page for the operator.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Framed 1885 Ulysses S. Grant "In Memoriam" printed fringed silk/textile from Memorial Services, City Park, Dayton, Ohio, Saturday Aug 8 1885 - period regional memorial piece — Confirm it is printed silk (not modern paper repro), check staining/tears and the left panel text; larger Dayton-specific piece is scarcer than standard ribbons. Buy under ~$150.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Pair of Chinese blue-and-white "Double Happiness" (shuangxi) jars with later wood lids, likely late Qing 19th c — Turn over: want unglazed sandy/orange-toned foot ring, kiln grit, slightly bluish glaze, hand-painted irregular scrolls; reject if bright white glaze, glazed base, or stenciled-looking uniform painting (modern Jingdezhen repro). Check rims for chips/hairlines. Pair under ~$150 is a buy.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Leica screw-mount rangefinder (III-series, knurled chrome dial visible) in original brown Leitz ever-ready case — Open case: model (IIIc/IIIf), serial, lens (Elmar/Summitar/Summicron), shutter firing at all speeds, fungus/haze; also check rest of the "collection of cameras" for Leitz lenses. Pass if tagged over ~$200 for body+Elmar

estate-sale golden-egg review: Andy Warhol / Paul Morrissey / Viva event poster, University of St. Thomas (Houston), 1968, hand-signed "Andy Warhol 68" in marker plus "Viva!" signature; water staining at lower margin — Close-up of signature in listing suggests company knows it is signed - expect a real price; worth buying under ~$500. Check signature is ink (not printed), dated 68, provenance story (attendee at UST/Menil 1968 event), staining extent, full poster image. Sale moved offsite to warehouse; address released Fri Oct 16 9am; sale Sat-Sun 9-1. Authentication (JSA/PSA) needed before res

estate-sale golden-egg review: VEB Freiberger Prazisionsmechanik (East German) micrometer-drum marine sextant, cream frame, scope, wooden box, blue certificate/manual (owner name "Walker Brents" written on frame) — Buy at $200 or less. Make sure mirrors are unsilvered/clean and not cracked, the drum turns smoothly, the telescope is present (the black piece in the box), and the certificate is in the lid. Owner name is written in marker on the frame, which hurts value a little.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Blickensderfer No. 7 portable typewriter (c.1897-1916) with original oak base and Blickensderfer-labeled bentwood case — Buy at $150 or less. Make sure the typewheel is present (the missing-wheel ones lose most of their value), the keys depress and the wheel rotates, the case lid and lock are complete, and there is no heavy rust. Note whether the keys are yellow; yellow keys are rarer.

estate-sale golden-egg review: American Airlines eagle-and-AA round dimensional sign, about 3 ft, red ring with raised blue eagle and letters — Decide whether it is original or a decorator reproduction. Original: molded fiberglass or acrylic with mounting hardware, a fabricator label on the back, and real wear on the paint. Reproduction: MDF/CNC wood or thin plastic with no label. Buy at $250 or less if original, otherwise pass. Measure it against the passenger seat (about 36 in diameter).

estate-sale golden-egg review: Jaeger-LeCoultre Atmos clock, cal. 540 "Classique" (Swiss, gilt case, skeleton dial), with a 1981 presentation plaque engraved to James L. Basham — Buy only if the price is under about $350. The caption does not name it, but Cottage Classics is a high-end gallery sale and may know what it is. Check that the balance wheel (the rotating torsion pendulum) turns, that the movement is locked (lever under the base), that the glass is not cracked and the case corners are not dented. The plaque lowers the value; it can be unscrewed.

estate-sale golden-egg review: Chest of about 60 pieces of ornate Baroque-pattern flatware, looks like Wallace Grande Baroque; it could be sterling or a silverplate copy (Godinger and others) — The photo is dark and the marks cannot be read. Flip a fork: if it is stamped "Wallace Sterling" or "Sterling", it is worth $1,500 or more just for the silver weight, so buy if the price is anything near silverplate pricing. If it is stamped Godinger, silverplate, EP or IS, walk away. David C. Turner is a professional company, so sterling will probably be priced as sterling.

eBay golden-egg review: Wally Shoop (b.1941, Cherokee-American) 'Spirit I (Eagle Catcher)' patinated bronze, signed & dated '86 on walnut plinth, ~24"H — Not an egg: the artist is named in the title, and comps run $325-1,300 (median ~$600). Blue spray-paint overspray on the plinth can be refinished. Shipping isn't listed, and a heavy bronze costs ~$60+ to ship in. Ended 20:09Z, before this review finished, so the price may already be settled.

eBay golden-egg review: Chinese blue-and-white ovoid ginger jar, bold lotus-scroll (Indian lotus) body under a key-fret shoulder band, unglazed mouth rim, glazed recessed base with chatter marks and iron spotting; 18th-19th c. Qing type, no lid — Not an egg: realistic value is $400-800 if period, and Jingdezhen reproductions of this exact pattern are common. The listing gives no size, and the description is boilerplate. At $175 + $22 shipping the margin is thin, so only buy at or below $175. Ends 20:44Z.

finds.title: Vintage costume Brooch/Pin
finds.note: text-triage F4: 1940s-50s open-backed pink baguette paste leaf brooch, prong-set, rollover clasp, 3.5in; no mark visible in photos. Worth it only if signed Trifari (crown T / "Sterling") or Coro Craft sterling - ask for a close photo of the stem and pin bar for a signature and "Sterling" stamp. Unsigned = ~$20 (no comp) -> pass.

finds.title: Vintage Sterling Silver Screw Back Earrings
finds.note: text-triage F2: 1940s retro tulip screwback earrings: blue faceted glass + 2 clear rhinestones each, seller says sterling (tarnish consistent). Lens: Coro. Ask for sharp photo of the back/screw mechanism: "STERLING" + maker (Coro Craft Pegasus, Trifari crown, Mazer, Reja, Boucher). Unsigned sterling ~$25-40 = kill; signed Trifari/Coro Craft sterling ~$60-100. Seller local only (Cle Elum WA), no ship.

finds.title: 1920's MILITARY STYLE WOMENS WATCH...REDUCED...
finds.note: text-triage F2: 1920s ladies cushion-case wristwatch, engraved white-metal bezel, 24-hour enamel/guilloche dial w/ sub-seconds, BOTH HANDS MISSING, $45. Ask for photo inside the case back: "14K"/"18K" solid (karat + assay, no "filled/GF/25 year") vs "14K gold filled". Solid 14K white-gold case (~3-5 g) -> est ~$150 low (case melt carries it); gold-filled -> kill (~$25).

finds.title: 14K Gold Necklace with Beautiful Christian Cross
finds.note: text-triage F5: 14K Italy S-link (serpentine) chain - partial "14K/ITALY" tag visible at clasp in photo 7; cross is plated (seller). Seller says 7.5 g but that likely includes the cross; a thin 18in serpentine chain is usually 2-4 g. Ask: scale photo of the CHAIN ALONE with 14K tag legible. Buy chain-only at $175 only if >=7 g (melt ~$55-75/g); at 3 g it is ~$180 melt = kill. Offer ~$140.

finds.title: knife collection
finds.note: text-triage F2: Lot of ~22 folders: 2 Victorinox, Wenger (green), Schrade Old Timer, Barlow (marked BARLOW bolster), red jigged-bone stockman, black jigged w/ shield, celluloid/MOP pens, Franklin Mint #24 Gordon. $50. Ask for tang-stamp close-ups of the red jigged stockman, the black shield knife, the bone/celluloid pens and the Barlow: looking for Case XX / Case Tested, Remington, Robeson, Ka-Bar, Camillus pre-1950 (not Imperial/Kutmaster/Colonial). Est $90 low as a lot -> profit only ~$8 unless one of those marks shows.

finds.title: Glass Vase
finds.note: text-triage F3: 7" blown clear vase with amber/red threaded veils, rough frosted base, diamond-scribed signature + "88" that neither seller nor photo resolves. Ask for a straight-on, in-focus shot of the full signature. A known studio name (e.g. Lotton, Eickholt) clears at $25; a generic regional signature (~$30–60) does not. no comp

finds.title: JEWELRY NECKLACES AND CHAINS
finds.note: text-triage L1: ~45 unmarked gold- and silver-tone chains + 2 graduated faux pearl strands with filigree clasps, $2 each (~$90 all). Seller says most unmarked. Ask: close-ups of every clasp/tag for 10K/14K/585, 925, or 1/20 12K GF stamps, and the pearl-strand clasps (14K filigree clasps are common on 1950s strands). Buy only marked solid-gold/sterling pieces at $2.

finds.title: JEWELRY RINGS
finds.note: text-triage F1: Costume ring lot priced $1-5 each (photos 4-12 all costume), BUT body lists 'two class rings priced at $10 each' which are not pictured. Gold egg if solid 10K/14K: a man's 10K class ring is typically 8-15g. Ask for: photo of inside shank stamps (10K/14K + maker Balfour/Jostens/Herff Jones/ArtCarved) vs base-metal alloys 'Lustrium', 'Siladium', 'Celestrium', 'Valadium', 'Ultrium', and weight in grams. Kill if alloy. No sold comp in db - est low $150 for one 10K ring (melt-driven).

finds.title: Peace Dove in Flight Glass Vintage Pendant
finds.note: text-triage F3: Frosted-glass dove on ribbed clear crescent with gold bail = the Nina Ricci "L'Air du Temps" dove motif (Lens: Nina Ricci frosted dove pendant); seller does not name Nina Ricci/Lalique. Ask for a photo of the back/bail: acid-etched "Lalique France" or "Nina Ricci" mark. Only a Lalique-signed piece clears the bar; unsigned promo pendant ~$40–60 does not. no comp

finds.title: Elgin pocket watches
finds.note: text-triage F3: Two "working" Elgin pocket watches with gold-tone fob for $200: (top) 18s key-wind open-face, silver-color case, key on string; (bottom) Elgin 12/16s open-face, yellow case. At $200 the bar is profit ≥ $200 (resale ≈ $480+), which only a solid gold case meets. Ask for photos inside both case backs ("14K"/"10K"/"Coin"/"Sterling" vs "Guaranteed 20/25 years"/"Keystone") and the movements (jewel count, grade). Sold comp: Elgin 14K hunter-case median $570; GF Elgins $40–150

finds.title: Vintage 21” Crash Cymbal
finds.note: text-triage F5: 21in old B20-looking cymbal, NO brand visible in any of 4 photos; Lens "Istanbul Agop" unverified (mismatch). Ask: photo of any stamp/ink on top and underside near the bell and edge (Zildjian trans-stamp/Avedis, Istanbul K, Paiste 602, UFIP), weight in grams, and confirm no cracks. Old trans-stamp A Zildjian 21in ride ~$250 low end (no comp); an Istanbul K would be multiples. Unstamped/Turkish-made no-name = kill.

finds.title: Original artwork
finds.note: text-triage F2: Framed abstract print "Silhouette", pencil-signed Artist's Proof, signature reads approx "D.A. Kono..sky" (unresolved); stained mat. Ask: artist full name/any gallery label on back, medium (serigraph/monotype), sight size. Only worth it if the name resolves to a listed printmaker; Lens $450 med is a category match. No comp.

finds.title: Vintage Link Bracelets
finds.note: text-triage L2: Chinese export nephrite (green) and mother-of-pearl (white) curved-link bracelets with pierced shou/fu character connectors and safety chain. Value hinges entirely on metal: 14K gold versions (~3-4g each) are worth $150-250 at gold melt; gold-filled/plated ones are the $50 ones the seller screenshotted. No karat mark visible in 13 photos. ASK: close-up of the box clasp tongue and end caps for "14K"/"585" vs "GF"/unmarked. Only proceed if 14K (then $90 both is a buy-tier lead). No comp. If both 14K: est $300 (no comp, gold-melt floor) -> 300*.87-10-10-90 = $151 profit; if GF/plated: kill (~$50 each asking).
